historical_record.description: Bay City Iron Works and a vacant lot occupied the 129 Fremont Street and 345 Mission Street parts of this site from 1887 to about 1889; the N. H. Cook Belting Company, a maker of leather belts, machine shops and offices followed, and by 1913 a machine shop and a foundry. The present building dates from 2009.

From about 1887 to 1899 the 124 Beale Street and 301 Mission Street parts of this site held machine shops, boiler works, offices, the Dow Steam Pump Works, a restaurant, a kitchen and a wagon room; by 1899 T. J. Moynahan's Boiler Works and the Dow Steam Pump Works had taken over both. The present building dates from 2009.
By 1913 W. P. Fuller & Co., dealers in paints, oils and glass, and a machine shop occupied this site; the buildings became offices after about 1970.

A building at 129 Fremont Street, on this site, was a foundry and blacksmith shop in 1913; the site's occupants in 1915 included a horseshoer and the Price Brothers firm of draymen. The present building dates from 2009.
The western half of the W. P. Fuller & Company Building, of reinforced concrete clad in brick, was built here to designs by George Applegarth.

The Walton N. Moore Dry Goods Warehouse was built at 129 Fremont Street, on this site: a reinforced-concrete structure with an open loft plan and a gable roof. Its architect is not known. The present building dates from 2009.

A six-storey fireproof reinforced-concrete warehouse, known as the Dry Goods Warehouse, was built at 124 Beale Street, on this site, by a real estate developer as an investment; it was later converted to offices. Its architect is not known. The present building dates from 2009.

The front of the 129 Fremont Street building then on this site, clad in green ceramic veneer above a black marble base, may have been remodelled in the late 1930s or the 1940s. The present building dates from 2009.

The Walton N. Moore Dry Goods Company, a wholesaler with a showroom at 345 Mission Street, bought the neighbouring 129 Fremont Street building as its warehouse; both stood on this site. The present building dates from 2009.
From 1970 until about 1989 the buildings then at 129 Fremont Street and 345 Mission Street, on this site, were Pacific Gas and Electric Company offices. The present building dates from 2009.
The building at 105-109 Fremont Street, on this site, was wholly or partly demolished between 1979 and October 1982. The present building dates from 2009.

The nine-storey building at 345 Mission Street, on this site, was damaged in the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake and then demolished; its basement was filled with the debris and the lot stood fenced and vacant. The present building dates from 2009.
The Redevelopment Agency photographed the property then on this site at 124 Beale Street. The present building dates from 2009.
The site then held three existing two- to six-story structures totaling about 173,650 gross square feet.
The City Planning Commission certified the final environmental impact report for the 301 Mission Street project.
The City Planning Commission adopted the CEQA findings for the 301 Mission Street project under Planning Code Section 309.
The 301 Mission Street site also contained a vacant parcel, the former site of a 126,732-square-foot office building demolished after the Loma Prieta earthquake.

The City Planning Commission approved, as amended, the Section 309 determinations and exceptions for the 301 Mission Street project, including working with the property owner at 201 Mission Street to facilitate removal of the pedestrian bridge and escalator at Beale and Mission Streets.
The City Planning Commission approved, with conditions as amended, the conditional use authorization for a major non-accessory parking garage and hotel use at 301 Mission Street.
The City Planning Commission approved as amended the Section 309 determinations of compliance and rear yard exception for the modified project at 301 Mission Street.
The Millennium Towers, a residential high-rise completed 2006-2009.
